quote: But I have a specialist in the area who can bring that over and help you take a look at the solar programs. Are you available as soon as tomorrow?
stewart_read: Rep skips the verify_section beat entirely — no re-confirmation of address/homeowner status, no interest question, no bill discussion — and jumps straight to booking tomorrow, treating this like a pure re-book rather than re-qualifying a customer who sounds unfamiliar with why Ion is calling.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: since this is a recycled/missed-appointment lead, the rep may be relying on prior intake data and intentionally skipping re-verification to save time. But the customer's confusion ('Is this the one which one is this?') shows the shortcut cost clarity rather than saved it.
coaching_implication: On recycled leads, spend 15-20 seconds re-anchoring what was discussed before, especially the reason for interest and the bill, before asking for a time — this would have prevented the confusion that opens the call.

quote: Is this the one which one is this? I've done a few of them, and none of the numbers ever came back worth shit.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a direct cost-skepticism objection tied to prior bad quotes — a textbook opening for the objection_inversion move (their bad past numbers are the reason THIS design matters). Rep does not address the skepticism at all and instead repeats the scheduling ask.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is the better fit here — there's no evidence the rep deliberately deferred; the rep simply pivots straight past the comment to logistics ('We never actually got a chance to meet with you...').
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to acknowledge burned-out skepticism directly ('sounds like the other numbers didn't work for you — that's exactly why we want to run your actual bill') before pushing a date.

quote: Is this one of those ones where, you I'm taking out a loan against my house, and the loan payment essentially is what you're balancing off of what my current electrical bill is?
stewart_read: Customer asks a direct trust question about the financing mechanism. Rep's answer ('No loans are announced. No liens.') is garbled and doesn't clearly confirm or deny a lien/loan structure, leaving the actual mechanism unresolved — the same honest-specificity principle used for 'how did you get my number' should apply here (be specific, not vague) but the rep is vague.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic deferral is unlikely — this is a factual product question the rep should be equipped to answer clearly on a setter call, not something to intentionally defer.
coaching_implication: Rep needs a clean one-line answer for the loan/lien mechanism question so a suspicious customer gets clarity, not confusion, on a topic this sensitive to trust.

quote: Nothing upfront. But there's a loan. Correct?
stewart_read: This is the second time the customer asks essentially the same lien/loan question because the first answer didn't land. Rep again says 'No. No.' before pivoting to describe financing options and the no-cost program, still without directly confirming whether a loan or lien is used.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive — there is no indication of an intentional deferral strategy; the rep appears to genuinely struggle to give a crisp answer.
coaching_implication: This is a repeat-touch on the same trust question; flag for the manager as a scripting/knowledge gap to fix directly, since the closer will need to resolve this same ambiguity.

quote: Yeah. Well, you can do that and and ring me next week, make sure everything's good to go.
stewart_read: The customer accepts a tentative Saturday appointment but frames it around a confirmation call next week — a real, customer-stated condition on the booking, not just a procedural gap. This should travel to the closer as a live condition.
coaching_implication: Handoff brief should flag that this appointment is conditional on a confirmation call, and the confirm call itself is critical to prevent a no-show.

quote: Alright. Saturday the eighteenth at twelve.
stewart_read: Rep states the day/time but never runs the verbal handshake ('Is that fair?'), never states the one-hour block, and never gives the no-driving/computer instruction — the appointment is set mechanically without the confirmation elements the schema flags as predictive of show rate.
coaching_implication: Add the full button-up sequence (hour block, no-driving-at-computer instruction, explicit fairness check) even on a call that's run long and the customer is cooperative — these mechanics are what protect the show rate.

quote: Thank you. Thank you, Joseph. Bye bye.
stewart_read: The rep closes the call by thanking the customer as 'Joseph' when the customer identified himself as 'Scott' at the very start of the call — a distinct, concrete error separate from the missing handshake mechanics.
coaching_implication: Flag as a standalone, easily-fixed error: confirm the customer's name before sign-off, especially on calls with multiple scheduling back-and-forths where attention may lapse.
